notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: Friday has no EGX session, so the latest close is Thursday 12 November (EGX30 52,023.37). Brent is Thursday's settlement and Friday's 02:42 GMT price. The pound is the banks' 1:36 pm quote on Thursday, as no CBE closing rate was found. Gold prices in EGP are Amwal Al Ghad's Thursday afternoon prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Thursday's investor flows, which Amwal Al Ghad gives in billions of pounds (about EGP 18.5 bn of foreign net buying), far out of line with normal sessions, so the flows chart is dropped; Thursday's breadth and turnover; a second source for Thursday's index closes (only Amwal Al Ghad was found, though the StockAnalysis closes move in line); the CBE's Thursday rate; Brent against the budget's oil assumption; the reserves split between foreign currency and gold. Gold in EGP: Amwal Al Ghad's Thursday article stamps its prices '16:14 on Monday', which conflicts with its headline; its prices (21K at EGP 5,975) are below Banky's Thursday morning prices (21K at EGP 6,115), in line with world gold's fall that day, so the brief uses Amwal's later prices and shows no daily change.
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Friday and show Thursday 12 November as the latest session; Palm Hills shows no change and is entered as 0. Thursday's index closes come from one source.

items: Israel's security cabinet orders the army to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, and Tehran threatens bases from West Asia to Europe → a renewed war would hit oil, Gulf shipping and the pound just as markets price a wind-down.
Eastern Company's nine-month profit rises 39% to about EGP 9 bn, and the stock gains 4.17% → sales rise 11% and margins widen, which supports the stock.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,500 on Wednesday after two days of gains, with turnover at EGP 11.79 bn → the rally pauses as small caps take profits; fertiliser stocks rebound.
The government targets public debt of about 69.5% of GDP by 2030 and frees a Red Sea plot to help pay it down → lower debt would ease debt-service costs over time.
EGX30 jumps 2.08% to 52,483 on Tuesday, a second day of gains, with EFG Holding up 6.75% → slower inflation and foreign buying of Egyptian T-bills lift sentiment.
Remittances rise 20.4% to a record $13 bn in July to September, and reach $38.2 bn in the first nine months of 2026 → the largest source of dollars for Egypt keeps growing despite the regional war.
Hotter US inflation and a hawkish Waller make a December Fed hike nearly certain → a higher US rate narrows the carry on Egyptian debt and lifts the cost of Egypt's floating-rate loans.
Foreign investors buy about $614.7 mn of Egyptian T-bills on Monday while selling stocks → the carry trade returns, which supports the pound.

Urban inflation slows to 12.7% in October from 13.9%, a nine-month low, while core inflation eases to 13.1% → the CBE's 20% deposit rate is now about 7.3 points above inflation (derived), giving it room to hold on 17 December.
Brent falls 5.85% on Monday and trades at $91.88 on Tuesday after Trump calls the Iran war effectively over → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound.
EGX30 rises 1.19% to 51,415 on Monday, but foreigners net sell EGP 302.9 mn → local investors drive the gains while foreign money takes profits.
Egypt Aluminum's quarterly profit more than doubles to EGP 4.93 bn → profit grows far faster than sales, which supports the stock's valuation.

The government raises gas cuts to fertiliser and methanol plants to 33% from 20% and notifies Ezz Steel of a 30% cut, with no end date → Asian LNG prices jump about 36% in a month, so Egypt saves gas for power and defers five of 15 November cargoes.
Abu Qir Fertilizers falls 5.78% and MOPCO 5.85% on Sunday as the EGX30 slips 0.67% to 50,812 → the gas cuts hit output at Egypt's largest urea exporters just as urea prices rise.
Evergreen's Ever Eon crosses the Suez Canal on Sunday, the line's first transit in nearly three years → the return of another major carrier supports canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Brent falls 1.5% to $96.91 in Asia on Monday as Trump says new strikes on Iran are very unlikely while talks progress → a US land blockade is now in effect, but de-escalation hopes outweigh new shipping attacks.

Egypt's annual headline inflation eases to 12% in October from 12.8% in September, with monthly inflation at 0.6% → slower inflation after the CBE's 100 bp hike widens the real rate and supports the case for holding rates.
Goldman Sachs says the pound is more than 30% undervalued and sees it at 50 per dollar in 12 months → a top bank's buy call can draw carry-trade money back into Egyptian debt.
The cabinet raises export rebates by an average of 35% and covers up to half of freight costs to new markets → the EGP 48 bn programme aims to lift exports and bring in more dollars.

The US sets up a task force to cut Iran's land supply routes as more blasts hit Qeshm and two tankers strike mines near Hormuz → the war widens even as Qatar-mediated talks continue, keeping oil and shipping risk high.

stories.h: Oil jumps 3.3% as Houthis hit Saudi sites and Iran strikes a US radar in Bahrain
stories.what: Brent settles $3.06 higher at $95.82 and WTI $2.21 higher at $88.74 on Thursday. Yemen's Houthis claim strikes on an East-West pipeline pumping station, a Yanbu oil facility and an Aramco building in Riyadh, and Iran's military says four tankers are hit in Hormuz. The IRGC says it targets a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. On Friday Brent is at $95.41, set for a 2.4% weekly fall, after Trump says a deal with Iran is not needed to end the war and the blockade stays.
stories.why: "Investors are growing weary from hearing the same song on peace prospects," says Matador Economics' Timothy Snyder.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping, the Red Sea and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: Oil near $96 raises Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound.
stories.egx: Bearish for importers and energy users; mildly bullish for oil-linked names.

key.l: spot gold's fall so far this week

stories.h: Gold hits a 13-month low as markets price a December Fed hike
stories.what: Spot gold rebounds 1% to $3,915 on Friday morning after a 13-month low on Thursday, and is down 3.5% this week. Markets fully price a quarter-point Fed hike in December and some weigh a half-point move; the dollar index is at 103.21. In Egypt, Amwal Al Ghad puts 21K gold at EGP 5,975 a gram and the gold pound at EGP 47,800 on Thursday afternoon, with the ounce at $3,890.
stories.why: Hot US inflation and higher oil push up rate expectations and the dollar.
stories.aff: Local gold prices, jewellers and household savings.
stories.eg: Lower gold prices cut the cost of a common savings asset for Egyptians.
stories.egx: Neutral for the EGX; a stronger dollar is a risk for the pound.

stories.h: EGX30 slips 0.91% to 52,023 as blue chips take profits
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; StockAnalysis.com; Arab Finance
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.91% to 52,023.37 on Thursday while the EGX70 rises 0.43% and the EGX100 0.14%; market cap is about EGP 4.17 tn. Housing and Development Bank (+5.79%) and QNB Egypt (+1.34%) gain, while Juhayna (-2.31%), Talaat Moustafa (-2.04%) and Telecom Egypt (-1.49%) fall. The dollar eases to EGP 53.46 at NBE.
stories.why: Investors lock in gains after the index rose about 3.3% from Sunday's close to Wednesday (derived).
stories.aff: Blue chips, banks and small caps.
stories.eg: A firm pound and steady local buying keep the market near its highs.
stories.names: Housing and Development Bank, QNB Egypt (up); Juhayna, Talaat Moustafa, Telecom Egypt (down).

stories.h: Suez Canal Bank's nine-month profit rises 12.9% to EGP 5.7 bn
stories.what: Suez Canal Bank's net profit rises 12.86% to EGP 5.7 bn in January to September 2026 from EGP 5.05 bn. Net interest income rises to EGP 8.793 bn from EGP 6.152 bn.
stories.why: Arab Finance gives no breakdown; interest income grows much faster than profit.
stories.eg: Banks keep benefiting from the CBE's high-rate stance.
stories.egx: Bullish for Suez Canal Bank and mid-sized banks.

stories.h: Civil aviation earns $4.8 bn in FY2025/26 as airports expand
stories.what: Civil Aviation Minister Sameh Elhefny tells President Sisi the sector generates $4.8 bn in FY2025/26. New airports at Alamein, Sphinx and the New Capital are expected to add about 12 mn passengers a year, and the first phase of Cairo Airport's Terminal 4 lifts capacity to 70 mn.
stories.why: The minister briefs the president on revenue and new airport capacity.
stories.aff: Airlines, airports, hotels and FX income.
stories.eg: More airport capacity supports the government's tourism targets.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for tourism and hospitality names.
